sources.note: Enahara variety (Ilha de Moçambique), not Moniga. §2.2 Prosody pp. 28-35: 'Makhuwa is clearly a tonal language'; 'Makhuwa does not have this penultimate lengthening' (p. 34). No word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Kröger, Oliver. 2005. Report on a survey of coastal Makua dialects. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2005-020. Dallas: SIL International. 45 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey; the only accessible work with Emoniga data (§3.4 pp. 18-19: Pebane district, c. 200,000 speakers, 62% cognates with Emakuana, 56% with Lomwe). No prose statement on stress, accent or tone in any dialect. Appendix 'Diagnostic list' pp. 41-42 and Table 1 p. 9 give IPA transcriptions ('phonetic transcript according to IPA conventions', p. 42) in which the primary-stress mark stands before the penultimate syllable in all 16 marked Emoniga items (‘máDi 'water', nta’íko 'tree', mu’lámu 'brother-in-law', ma’rúpo 'intestines', e’sikó 'neck', ‘múthu 'person'..); acute marks ton…

sources.citation: Kisseberth, Charles W. 2003. Makhuwa (P30). In Nurse & Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 546-565. London: Routledge.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The source named by the earlier scan (Glottolog cites it only for subclassification). Dialect survey §2 names no Moniga/Pebane variety; data from Ikorovere and Imitthupi (Tanzania). §3.4 Tone pp. 553-555: no lexical tone contrasts in verbs, H assigned by morphology; H doubling blocked phrase-finally and on the second mora of a bimoraic phrase-penult syllable. The words 'stress', 'accent' and 'penultimate lengthening' do not occur in the chapter; nothing on Emoniga.
